master_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target: the supplied Listening Room image from The Ninth Tide.
User-approved revision direction: replace the three huge empty cork panels with a smaller working noticeboard; make the recorder recognizable and prominent; give the room a purpose-built recording bench; add restrained human wear; retain the important sea window and add warm local task light; a faint damp seat impression is the first unsettling detail.

Create ONE polished revised full-room illustration, same 1448 x 1086 / 4:3 framing. Preserve the LEFT BLUE DOOR, RIGHT SEA WINDOW with rainy water/lighthouse, sage plaster, blue wainscoting, floor and flat front-facing composition in their existing locations. Same fine navy ink contours, broad matte colors, subtle paper grain, restrained brass, warm brown wood. Absolutely no horns, speaking trumpets, ornate wall apparatus, angled walls, vanishing points, receding desktop planes or photorealism.

Composition:
1. REMOVE all three giant cork panels. Restore sage plaster. Replace them with ONE modest rectangular dark-wood-framed cork noticeboard, about 400 pixels wide by 260 tall, centered above the recorder around x=760,y=340. Leave generous sage wall around it. On it pin a slightly crooked cream recording log with a few neat columns, a smaller handwritten correction slipped over its corner, and one small curled sepia photograph showing two station workers by the coast. Add subtle pinholes and a pale mark from a removed paper. The papers should feel handled, not like decorative scrapbook clutter. No legible puzzle answers, no exact labels, no readable dates or numbers: final evidence is authored separately.

2. REDESIGN the big office-style desk into a purpose-built narrow oak recording bench, maintaining its approximate footprint below the wall board and leaving both door and window clear. Front elevation only: its working surface is a narrow horizontal strip, not an angled tabletop. LEFT SIDE: four shallow full-width cylinder drawers stacked vertically with small brass label holders. RIGHT SIDE: one open rectangular storage compartment with a few horizontal cylindrical storage cases and a thin ledger on a lower shelf. Use clear flat silhouettes with no perspective shelf sides. Center is a open knee space with the blue wall visible, making the furniture lighter and distinct from the Intake Office desk. No symmetrical office drawer pedestals or giant decorative central door panel.

3. The MAIN FOCAL OBJECT on the bench is now a larger unmistakable HORNLESS wax-cylinder recording/playback machine in flat side elevation. A substantial dark oak plinth and a compact brass drive housing support a thick dark honey-brown grooved recording cylinder. Show TWO short adjoining wax sleeves seated on its spindle, with the THIRD matching loose sleeve clearly visible in a small open storage case beside it. This is a partially assembled visual study, not the locked new-game configuration. The needle arm visibly rests over the grooved wax; add a clear small winding crank on the right and a simple transport lever on the plinth. Do not make it look like an exposed empty lathe. The cylinder and needle must read at room scale. No horn or large cone anywhere. Precise seam geometry and C/A/B markings will be added separately, so do not generate those clues.

4. Hang the modest old black leather-and-ebonite HEADPHONES from a simple peg just left of the small noticeboard, within reach of someone at the bench. The headband has a tiny stitched repair, subtly visible. Their cloth cord leads down to the recorder. Add a small brush, a few wax shavings around it, and a visibly rubbed elbow patch on the narrow wooden bench edge. Keep props limited and purposeful. Retain the existing upright cream instruction card at the right of the recorder, with a discreet suggested diagram but no legible writing.

5. Add ONE small practical shaded brass task lamp fixed to the left end of the recording bench. A modest low hood, not a flared horn shape. It casts a restrained warm amber pool across the cylinder, wax pieces and hands' working area. Render the warmth as broad subtle flat color, not a cinematic beam or volumetric glow. The rest stays cool and softly lit by the important right-hand storm window. The warm recorder should attract the eye first, the window second.

6. Preserve the worn wooden stool near the left half of the bench, front elevation. On its seat add a FAINT irregular darker damp oval where someone would have sat. No puddle on the floor, no dripping water, no human outline or spectral body. The headphones, surrounding cork and other furniture remain dry. A small intimate wrongness, easy to miss until examined.

Overall: a convincing abandoned recording workplace, tangible and lived-in, with focused detail around the machine and quiet wall space elsewhere. Dark maritime atmosphere through restraint. NO skulls, eyes, blood, tentacles, runes, theatrical horror props, modern screens, additional maps, captions, UI, borders or watermark. Preserve clean room geometry and clue readability.
